A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GH-ESD and GESD, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. v4 retains the main article and adds supplementary Sections S1–S4, which are referenced but absent from the supplied v3.

before.justification: v3 reports original slice-discovery experiments, component ablations and model-repair outcomes in Section 5, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and supplies additional empirical results, including per-slice segmentation scores and model-selection and matching-score comparisons.

M1.justification: The grounded hypothesis construction, VLM matching, monotonic verification and model-repair procedures remain unchanged. The supplement documents previously referenced prompts, implementation choices and the interactive tool; it does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover GESD detection and segmentation, constructed from COCO, KITTI and face-detection data, plus Waterbirds, CelebA and NICO++. The supplementary results concern these existing tasks and datasets, without establishing additional coverage.

E2.justification: Section S3.1 adds reported component comparisons using GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet for hypothesis generation, and SigLIP and GPT-4o alongside Qwen2.5-VL-7B for matching. The main slice-discovery and repair comparator sets in Tables 1–4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added matching-score experiment evaluates alternative score constructions using mAP on a benchmark subset, while Table S1 reports matching speed per 1,000 images alongside Precision@10. These augment the reported evaluation design; the original benchmark and repair settings are not reported as revised.

E4.justification: Section S3.1 supplies substantive additional analyses of LLM choice, VLM precision–speed tradeoffs and matching-score construction. The latter compares yes/no logits, numerical outputs and categorical responses, reporting mAP of 0.47, 0.23 and 0.18. These substantially extend the available component evidence beyond the retained Section 5.2 ablations.

E5.justification: Section S3.1 newly reports five runs for the matching-score ablation. Section S3.5 clarifies randomized seeds and standard-deviation reporting for classification repair. The existing three-repetition detection repair and ten-run classification repair reports remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables S3–S4 add individual results for 21 detection and 21 segmentation slices, including segmentation average Precision@10 of 0.805 and one zero-scoring slice. Section S3.1 and Table S1 add model, speed and scoring-ablation results. Main Tables 1–4 are unchanged; detection Precision@10 of 0.729 is equivalent rounding of the retained 0.73, not a performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section S3.5 newly formalizes the repair group attribute, weighted detection-head and total losses, and exponential group-weight updates, where v3 describes the weighting verbally. The core matching and trend definitions remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about grounded instance-level discovery, the GESD benchmark, detection improvement and segmentation applicability. The added dataset-availability statement does not redefine the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations of limited sensitivity to LLM choice, the VLM efficiency tradeoff, and numerical-output instability versus categorical quantization. Section S3.3 also identifies the surfboard-on-land segmentation failure. The main discussion of dataset coverage and incomplete hypothesis spaces remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies generation, matching and evaluation prompts; the HiBug attribute corpus; checkpoint provenance; repair hyperparameters and loss implementation; and A100/vLLM execution details. It also adds a public-availability statement and repository address for GESD. These substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to existing implementations.

R1.justification: The supplement adds the PagedAttention/vLLM serving reference. Its LADDER and FACTS references repeat works already cited in v3. The main related-work discussion, novelty positioning and reference list are unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing main-paper wording and section order are essentially retained. v4 adds an availability sentence and organizes supporting material into supplementary Sections S1–S4, without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the main narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures S1–S14 and Tables S1–S4: prompt panels, dataset-distribution plots, detailed result and attribute tables, and interactive-tool screenshots. This substantially expands the visual documentation. Existing main figures and tables retain their content, with only limited early-page reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 repeatedly references supplementary prompts, implementation details and segmentation results that its supplied PDF does not contain. v4 resolves this important documentation gap, making the method substantially more reproducible and its segmentation evidence directly assessable. Additional component analyses and dataset-access information strengthen the paper while its main results and scientific claims remain stable.
